---
title: "History and Related Topics"
---

The Inferential Model idea was originally inspired by ideas from Dempster-Shafer calculus (itself inspired by Fiducial inference). In the Dempster Shafer framework, they create Belief functions -- an alternative way of describing evidence as opposed to probability. It was through the theory of Random Sets that the original IM solution came to be. 

Later realizing that assuming monotonicity in Random Sets (the evidence concentrates at the MLE) corresponds directly to possibility theory, the corresponding implementation has become much cleaner.
